alt: The prescribed passage, Qur’an 2:183-185, broken into five ideas: the command to fast, the purpose of taqwa, the concession for the ill and travellers, Ramadhan as the month of revelation, and the spirit of ease rather than hardship.
caption: Use the passage for purpose, compassion and the balance of obligation and mercy.

after: ## The rulings of a valid fast
alt: A day bar: suhoor is eaten before true dawn, the fast runs from Fajr to Maghrib with no food, drink or sexual relations and no lying, backbiting or anger, and iftar is taken promptly at sunset. A note explains the intention before dawn and the white and black thread of 2:187.
caption: The fast runs from true dawn to sunset, framed by suhoor and iftar.

alt: Acts that invalidate a fast and their effect: deliberate eating or drinking, deliberate sexual relations, which also requires kaffarah of sixty days’ fasting or feeding sixty poor people, deliberate vomiting, the start of menstruation, and smoking. Eating by genuine mistake does not break the fast.
caption: Deliberate acts break the fast; genuine forgetfulness does not.

after: ## Exemptions and what is owed afterwards
alt: Two groups of exemption. Qada, making up the days later: the temporarily ill, travellers, pregnant or breastfeeding women who fear harm, and women in menstruation or post-natal bleeding. Fidya, feeding a poor person for each day: the elderly and the chronically ill who will not recover (2:184). Children and the insane owe nothing.
caption: Qada makes up the days; fidya feeds the poor when fasting will never be possible.

alt: Benefits of fasting in three categories: spiritual, such as taqwa and more Qur’an recitation; moral, such as self-discipline, honesty and patience; and social, such as empathy with the hungry, charity and shared iftar. Health benefits are a side effect.
caption: Use the specification’s three headings: spiritual, moral and social.

alt: A strip of the thirty nights of Ramadhan: Taraweeh is prayed every night after Isha, Itikaaf is usually observed in the last ten days, and Laylat ul-Qadr is sought in the odd nights of the last ten. Cards explain Taraweeh, Itikaaf and Laylat ul-Qadr.
caption: Itikaaf in the last ten days keeps a Muslim in worship whenever Laylat ul-Qadr falls.
